papers.title_in_file: Chip-integrated Spectroscopy Capable of Temperature Retrieval
papers.what_it_is: A thin-film lithium niobate microring emission spectrometer with 2 pm resolution that retrieves source temperature from the K-line width of a hollow cathode lamp.
papers.why_not: A photonic-chip spectroscopy and plasma-temperature paper with no quantum computing, machine learning, finance or evaluation-method content; its assertions carry context method only because the field is required.

assertions.value: The authors state that the filter is a microring resonator on a 300-nm thin-film lithium niobate wafer etched to 180 nm, with ring radius R = 40 µm, and a simulated group index of 2.4038 at 770 nm giving a free spectral range of 0.98 nm by design.
quotes: we design and fabricate the circuits on a 300-nm TFLN wafer, shallow etched to a height of 180 nm. The ring radius is R = 40 µm.
For the center wavelength λ = 770 nm, the simulated group refractive index ng = 2.4038, so that the FSR is 0.98 nm by design.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section II states the device setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a resonance full width at half maximum of 2 pm in the fine scan, corresponding to a loaded Q of 0.38 × 106 (as printed, 0.38 times ten to the sixth).
quotes: The resonance profile has a FWHM of 2-pm as shown in the inset of Fig. 1(b), corresponding to a loaded cavity of Q = 0.38 × 106.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that fine-scan calibration of the tunable laser reduces the measurement error from 2 pm to 0.03 pm relative to their previous measurement, and that the laser resolution reaches 0.01 pm with a fluctuation of 0.03 pm.
assertions.anchor: Section II p.2; Appendix B p.8
quotes: reduce the measurement error from 2 pm to 0.03 pm [27].
we determine that the laser resolution reaches 0.01 pm with a fluctuation of 0.03 pm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report a thermo-optic tunability of 6.3691 pm/mW for a heater-to-waveguide distance of 2.8 µm, from a linear fit with coefficient of determination r2 = 1 over a voltage scan from 17 V to 26 V at 0.5 V steps.
quotes: The slope of the linear fitting line ∆λres/∆Ph indicates a tunability of 6.3691 pm/mW.
Figure 3 shows tunability of MRR with distance 2.8 µm used for our experiment.
The coefficient of fitting determination, r2 = 1, confirms the excellent linearity of the response.
we apply voltage manually from 17 V to 26 V, at a step size of 0.5 V.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report from Fig. 2 that when the heater-waveguide lateral distance exceeds 2.8 µm the linewidth is nearly not affected by metal absorption, while tunability remains sufficiently large for the experiment.
quotes: when the distance exceeds 2.8 µm, the linewidth is nearly not affected by metal absorption.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the filter, swept by heater voltage and read by a single-photon detector, resolved the potassium D2 and D1 lines at 766.5 nm and 769.9 nm, matching NIST database values, with a measured dark count of 147 ± 11 Hz.
quotes: The filtered wavelengths match well with the NIST database values of 766.5 nm and 769.9 nm [6]. The dark count is measured as 147 ± 11 Hz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the light source was a potassium hollow cathode lamp with neon fill driven at 8 mA and 280 V, and that detection used a single-photon counting module with a 1-second integration time per point.
quotes: We apply a current of 8 mA and a voltage of 280 V to generate an intense electric field between the lamp’s cathode and anode, where the inert Ne gas is ionized.
over a 1-second integration time to suppress Poissonian noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III states the experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the 3.4 nm spacing between the two K lines means only one line can pass the MRR at a time, and that the doublet was measured with a single chip but individually, not simultaneously.
assertions.anchor: Section II p.3; Section VI p.7
quotes: The spacing between the two is 3.4 nm, so that only one line can be transmitted by the MRR at a time
In this demonstration, we have measured the K doublet lines using a single chip but individually.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors as a limit of this demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors report that the measured emission linewidth increased as the lamp current was raised from 8 mA to 40 mA, with each linewidth measured three times and error bars given as the standard deviation of the three.
quotes: Therefore, the increase of linewidth is observed as we increase the lamp current.
For each applied lamp current, the linewidth measurement was repeated three times.
The lamp current is scanned from 8 mA to 40 mA.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that temperature is retrieved from the measured linewidth by modelling the observed profile as the convolution of a Gaussian (Doppler) profile, a lamp collision Lorentzian and the ring-resonator Lorentzian, with the Voigt FWHM taken from an approximation formula.
quotes: the FWHM of Voigt spectrum in Eq. (3) is then given to a very good approximation as [39]:
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The method is a model-based inversion; its accuracy depends on the assumed species fractions, radii and the Saha equilibrium assumption.

assertions.value: The authors state that the plasma model assumes a weakly ionized lamp plasma in local thermal equilibrium, a degeneracy ratio g1/g0 = 4, a neon first ionization energy of 21.56454 eV, and a total number density n = 1.61 × 1023 m−3 from the ideal gas law with p = 5 torr at T = 300 K.
quotes: Given that the lamp plasma is considered to be weakly ionized and assuming local thermal
equilibrium for particles in the glass tube
The degeneracy ratio of Neon ion to neutral Neon is given by g1/g0 = 4 [37]. The first ionization energy of Ne is ϵ = 21.56454 eV [38].
By using p = 5 torr at T = 300 K, the calculated total number density is n = 1.61 × 1023 m−3
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV lists the model assumptions and inputs.

assertions.value: The authors report that the retrieved temperature with the plasma model is on the same order of magnitude (×104 K, as printed) as a temperature retrieved by a Boltzmann plot in Ref. [29], and almost one order of magnitude lower than the model with no ionization.
quotes: perature is on the same order of magnitude (×104 K) of the temperature retrieved by Boltzmann plot in Ref. [29]
this retrieved temperature is almost one order of magnitude less than the model without considering plasma (completely unionized)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: No independent temperature measurement of the lamp is given; the comparison is to a different experiment in the cited work, so the retrieved temperature is not validated here.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the lamp, collision broadening from K-electron collisions dominates over K-neutral neon collisions, and above a specific current it even dominates Doppler broadening; K-Ne+ collisions are ignored as weaker than K-Ne.
quotes: it is evident that the collision broadening due to K-e collisions dominates over K-Ne collisions. Above specific current, it even dominates the doppler broadening.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report from their wildfire model that collision broadening exceeds Doppler broadening below 5910 K, and the composite linewidth is smallest at 5070 K; they note flaming combustion generally occurs below 2500 K, suggesting collision broadening predominates in wildfire.
quotes: below 5910 K (circular point), the collision broadening in wildfire play a more significant role than Doppler broadening.
At 5070 K (square point), the composited broadening is at the minimum.
Flaming combustion in wildland fuels generally occurs at temperatures below 2500 K [10]
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a model result at 760 torr with air composition; it was not tested on a real fire.

assertions.value: The authors report a finite-difference time-domain thermo-optic coefficient of 1.79 × 10−5 K−1 (as printed) and state a heated ring temperature range of 300-557 K for 0-32 V from the extracted heater efficiency.
quotes: In our case, ∂neff /∂T = 1.79 × 10−5 K−1.
The temperature range of the heated ring waveguide (300 − 557 K) is obtained by using the applied voltage range of 0-32 V and the extracted heater efficiency.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the 2 pm resolution is adequate to quantitatively measure line broadening for wildfire, fusion, star and AGN sources, based on a table of literature broadening ranges; they state different applications may need distinct circuit designs and retrieval models.
quotes: For all of them, the 2 pm FWHM spectral resolution of the current MRR devices is adequate to quantitatively measure the line broadening effects
distinct circuit designs and retrieval models may be required to achieve the optimal performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Only the potassium lamp was measured; the other sources are covered by literature values and simple models, not by experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the periodic transmission windows (FSR on the order of nanometers) admit photons from other windows, so a coarse filter is needed against broad background noise, and a tunable coarse filter narrower than the FSR could extend the measurement range.
assertions.anchor: Section II p.2; Section V p.6-7
quotes: In typical settings, FSR is on the order of nanometers, so that the filter will admit not only the target signal photons, but also those in other periodic windows.
the spectral measurement range can exceed the FSR by adding a tunable coarse filter with bandwidth narrower
assertions.certainty_reason: Section II states the limit of the filter.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they demonstrated a chip-integrated microring emission spectroscope measuring K lines from a lamp plasma with a 2 pm FWHM and a linewidth-based temperature retrieval method, and claim it offers high performance, low cost and robustness for airborne and spaceborne missions.
quotes: we have demonstrated a high-precision emission spectroscope using a chip-integrated microring resonator on thin-film lithium niobate
which measures the K lines from a HCL plasma source with a FWHM of 2 pm.
our device offers high performance, low cost, and robustness for airborne and spaceborne missions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The low-cost and robustness statements are not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state as future work coupling multiple MRRs to a single photon detector and sweeping them together for hyper-spectral measurement, and integrating components such as WDM, frequency converters, parametric amplifiers and single photon detectors on the same chip.
quotes: In the future, one can couple the outputs of multiple MRRs each to a single photon detector and sweep their resonance all at the same time, for hyper-spectral measurement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical or stated result of one study.
